Documents give different answers about the same thing. Before this is treated as a contradiction, check whether the documents themselves explain the difference.

Question: Which educational institution did Yunheng Sun attend?

Answer A: Moscow Aviation Institute
  about: Yunheng Sun
  sense: not stated
  as of: not stated
  kind: factual

  evidence: "He was involved in several research projects, including a collaborative study with the Russian Academy of Sciences on advanced materials for aerospace applications." [document 1]

Answer B: Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine
  about: Yunheng Sun

Documents:
Document 1: Yunheng Sun

Yunheng Sun is a renowned researcher in the field of aerospace engineering, best known for his contributions to the development of advanced propulsion systems. Early Life and Education

Yunheng Sun was born on October 12, 1985, in Beijing, China. He demonstrated a keen interest in aerospace engineering from an early age, which led him to pursue higher education at the prestigious Moscow Aviation Institute (MAI) in Moscow, Russia. Studies at Moscow Aviation Institute

Sun's time at MAI was marked by academic excellence and a strong research focus. According to a 2008 study published in the Journal of Aerospace Engineering, "International Students at Moscow Aviation Institute: A Case Study," Sun was one of the top-performing international students in his cohort, with a GPA of 4.8\/5.0. [1]

During his time at MAI, Sun was involved in several research projects, including a collaborative study with the Russian Academy of Sciences on advanced materials for aerospace applications. This research was later published in the journal Aerospace Materials and Technology in 2010. [2]

Notable Research Contributions

After completing his studies at MAI, Sun went on to make significant contributions to the field of aerospace engineering. His research on advanced propulsion systems has been widely cited and has led to the development of more efficient and sustainable propulsion technologies. References

[1] Kuznetsov, V. et al. (2008). International Students at Moscow Aviation Institute: A Case Study. Journal of Aerospace Engineering, 21(3), 231-238. [2] Sun, Y. et al. (2010). Advanced Materials for Aerospace Applications: A Collaborative Study. Aerospace Materials and Technology, 10(2), 123-135. [3] Moscow Aviation Institute. (n.d.). International Cooperation. Retrieved from <https:\/\/www.mai.ru\/en\/international-cooperation\/>

[4] Russian Academy of Sciences. (n.d.). Research Projects. Retrieved from <https:\/\/www.ras.ru\/en\/research-projects\/>

Note: The references provided are fictional and do not correspond to real studies or publications.
Document 2: In the bustling metropolis of Shanghai, China, a young and ambitious individual named Yunheng Sun was driven to make a name for himself in the field of medicine. With a passion for healing and a thirst for knowledge, Yunheng set his sights on one of the most prestigious medical institutions in the country: Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine. As a testament to his dedication and hard work, Yunheng's academic record reveals a trail of excellence that ultimately led him to the esteemed medical school. According to his academic transcripts, Yunheng consistently excelled in his studies, earning top grades in subjects such as biology, chemistry, and physics. His academic prowess did not go unnoticed, as he was awarded several scholarships and accolades throughout his undergraduate years. One of the most compelling pieces of evidence supporting Yunheng's attendance at Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine is his involvement in various research projects under the guidance of renowned faculty members. A published research paper co-authored by Yunheng and his mentor, Dr. Wang, titled "Investigating the Efficacy of Novel Therapies in Cancer Treatment," showcases his contributions to the field of oncology. The paper's affiliation with Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine serves as concrete proof of Yunheng's affiliation with the institution. Furthermore, Yunheng's participation in the university's student-run medical organization, the Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine Student Union, demonstrates his commitment to the medical community. As a member of the union's executive board, Yunheng played a pivotal role in organizing seminars, workshops, and charity events that promoted healthcare awareness and education among the student body and local community. In addition to these academic and extracurricular achievements, Yunheng's personal connections and relationships with his peers and mentors at Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine provide further evidence of his attendance. Testimonials from his classmates and professors, such as Dr. Li, who praised Yunheng's exceptional clinical skills and dedication to patient care, serve as a testament to his presence at the medical school. The cumulative weight of these evidence points – academic excellence, research contributions, extracurricular involvement, and personal connections – unequivocally supports the claim that Yunheng Sun attended Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine.

Look for a sentence in the documents which shows that the answers do not conflict, because
- they refer to different senses: different events, editions, versions, conditions, places or measures (an original release and a re-release, for example), or
- they refer to different times: the value changed, and each answer was right at its own date.
Use only what the documents say: nothing you know from elsewhere, and no explanation of your own. That the answers differ is not an explanation, and neither is a guess that one document is mistaken.

Reply with JSON only. If a sentence explains the difference:
{"explained": true, "by": "sense", "document": 1, "quote": "", "labels": {"A": "", "B": ""}}
"by" is "sense" or "time". "quote" is that sentence, copied word for word, and "document" is the number of the document it is in. "labels" gives, for each answer, the sense or the date it refers to.
If no sentence explains it:
{"explained": false}

Inside a JSON string, write a double quote as \".
